text: AI-assisted coding goes wrong in five predictable ways.
Editing a file it never read. A confident fix from a skim. Quietly drifting from the plan. A new helper instead of the existing one. And losing the thread when the context fills up.
Each one leaves a trace, in the session and in git.
Sensei names and counts them per repository, with the evidence behind each, so you can judge for yourself.

Better still, it heads them off: it grounds the task, checks the plan’s depth, searches for existing code, and keeps your rules through compaction. What slips through is caught, and your corrections become rules.
